title: Harmonize parallel cost-accounting paths post-OTC: hil_gate vs cost_cap.spend_for_edition_usd
description:
**Surfaced by:** Spec 2A Chunk 5 (F17) spec-compliance reviewer of commit `784d27d1`.

**Problem:** Two separate cost-accounting paths exist for edition cap enforcement, keyed differently:

1. `backend/app/services/agents/hil_gate.py:910-915` (`_check_caps_atomically`)
   - Keys off `agent_runs.edition_id` column
   - Now uses F17's `cost_charged_to_edition = TRUE` filter (post-Chunk 5)
   - Hot path for HIL gate enforcement

2. `backend/app/services/newsletter/cost_cap.py:114` (`spend_for_edition_usd`)
   - Keys off `input_digest LIKE 'edition:UUID:%'`
   - NOT touched by F17 (outside spec scope per §4.2 line 322)
   - Consumed by `preflight.py:150` and possibly other paths

**Risk:** F17's flag-based exclusion semantics (orphan-GC + operator-recoverable explicit-fail clear the flag) only apply to path #1. If preflight checks the SAME edition's cap via path #2, it sees the OLD `status IN ('running', 'success')` semantics, which would re-include orphaned pre-charges that path #1 has already excluded.

**Symptom this could cause:** A retry that hil_gate allows (because the failed attempt's `cost_charged_to_edition` was cleared) might be DENIED by preflight (because path #2 still sums the failed attempt's cost via input_digest match). This is a "cap drift" between layers.

**Verification needed post-OTC:**
1. Trace all callsites of `spend_for_edition_usd`. Determine if any are in the request-pre-flight or worker-pre-flight paths.
2. Decide between:
   - (a) Migrate `cost_cap.py:114` to use the same `cost_charged_to_edition = TRUE` filter (preferred)
   - (b) Document the divergence and accept it (only if path #2 is genuinely a different semantic — e.g., per-input-digest cap rather than per-edition cap)
3. If (a): add 1-2 regression tests covering the orphan-GC and operator-recoverable-error chains via path #2.

**Why deferred:** Spec 2A §4.2 line 322 explicitly scopes F17 to `hil_gate.py:906-941`. Touching `cost_cap.py` would expand scope. OTC May 4 deadline takes precedence.

**Spec reference:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-30-spec2a-otc-tactical-design.md` §4.2
**Source commit:** `784d27d1` (Chunk 5 F17 path-2)
acceptance_criteria: Either migrate cost_cap.py:114 to use cost_charged_to_edition flag (with regression tests) OR document the divergence with explicit rationale and verify both paths are exercised by integration tests.

title: Connection-pool-aware sandbox variant for write_audit + asyncio.gather tests (15 xfailed)
description:
## Background
C13.5 (commit pending) marked 15 tests in `tests/services/agents/` with `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` because they assert production-code correctness for behaviors that REQUIRE multiple independent connections, which the canonical SAVEPOINT sandbox (single connection) cannot model.

## Categories
- 12 tests: `write_audit` audit-row durability — production opens its OWN async_session() per the 2026-04-28 incident fix; sandbox can't see those rows because they commit on a different connection outside the SAVEPOINT scope.
- 3 tests: `asyncio.gather` concurrent gate calls — asyncpg refuses concurrent operations on a single connection.

## Files
- `tests/services/agents/test_audit.py` (1 test)
- `tests/services/agents/test_base_agent.py` (3 tests)
- `tests/services/agents/test_circuit_breaker.py` (1 test)
- `tests/services/agents/test_cumulative_input_budget.py` (1 test)
- `tests/services/agents/test_max_iterations.py` (1 test)
- `tests/services/agents/test_hil_gate.py` (8 tests: 5 audit/edition + 3 concurrent)

## Solution Sketch
Build a sandbox variant that allocates a real connection pool inside a per-test schema (or per-test database) so:
1. write_audit's independent async_session() lands in the same isolation scope as the test session
2. asyncio.gather can run concurrent operations on separate connections from the pool

Options:
- Per-test schema with search_path swap + connection pool pinned to that schema
- Per-test ephemeral database (slower; cleanest isolation)
- pytest-postgresql + asyncpg pool fixture

When implemented, REMOVE the xfail markers; strict=True will fail loudly, alerting that the architectural limitation is now solvable.

## References
- ci-recovery-c11.5 reviewer categorization
- ci-recovery-c13.5 commit (this commit)
- 2026-04-28 audit-row durability incident → write_audit independent-session refactor

title: Fleet-Map Phase 2: Gemini deep-research backlog (post-OTC)
description:
Items surfaced by Gemini deep-research doc `docs/research/Implementing AIS Data with MapLibre.md` that are NOT OTC-blocking but should ship before Posidonia (Jun 1). Wave 7 already covered the 3 OTC-critical items (rotation/pitch alignment, lat/long bounds, text-overlap).

## Backlog

### 1. AIS Type 24 multi-part Part A/B merge (Gemini §lines 27)
Class B vessels split static data into Part A (vessel name) and Part B (call sign + dimensions + type). Consumer must inspect `part_num` field and merge — common bug: Part B overwrites Part A and the name is lost. Currently our discovery consumer (`ais_consumer.py` AISDiscoveryConsumer) doesn't handle this. Most demo vessels are Class A (single-message), so OTC unaffected.

### 2. Native MapLibre clustering at zoom-out (Gemini §line 54)
At low zoom levels (regional/global view), 100+ vessels visually overlap into a soup. Add `cluster: true`, `clusterMaxZoom: 8`, `clusterRadius: 40` to GeoJSON source; cluster expands as user zooms in. GPU-accelerated via Supercluster.

### 3. Kinematic interpolation between AIS reports (Gemini §lines 67-78)
Vessels currently "teleport" between 30s polls. Add `requestAnimationFrame` interpolation: store target coords on update, smoothly transition via LERP (or Great Circle for poles). Major UX win — turns the demo from "static screenshot updates" to "fluid live tracking."

### 4. Differential GeoJSON updates / GeoJSONSourceDiff (Gemini §lines 40-46)
Replace `setData(newFeatureCollection)` with `GeoJSONSourceDiff` (additions/removals/updates) keyed on `promoteId: 'mmsi'`. Critical for scaling beyond ~200 vessels — naive `setData` triggers full re-tessellation in the WebWorker.

### 5. Reaper pattern with status-aware staleness thresholds (Gemini §lines 31-35)
Currently we have one global `MAX_POSITION_AGE_HOURS=6`. Per Gemini, threshold should be navigational-status-aware:
- High-speed underway: 3 minutes stale
- Anchored/moored tankers: 6+ hours stale
Plus hard-deletion at 24h to prevent unbounded vessel_positions growth (currently 21.5M rows).

### 6. Bounding box debouncing on viewport change (Gemini §lines 113-116)
Currently we always send global bbox. Phase 2: subscribe to MapLibre `moveend` event, debounce 500-1000ms, send updated bbox to backend → re-subscribe AIS WS with new geographic filter. Reduces network bandwidth dramatically when user zooms into a port.

### 7. Coordinate precision truncation (Gemini §line 48)
Truncate lat/lon to 6 decimal places (~11cm accuracy) before persistence. Saves ~30 bytes per row at 21.5M+ rows. Use `turf.truncate` or simple `round(x, 6)`.

### 8. Cold-start cache pre-hydration (Gemini §line 26)
When new client opens map, fetch vessel static data from a Redis cache (populated by AIS consumer continuously). Avoids ~6-min wait for next ShipStaticData broadcast cycle. Less critical for our case since `vessels` table already has full metadata for seeded demo fleet.</description>

title: Disk hygiene: auto-cleanup old release dirs (staging + prod)
description:
Old timestamped release directories accumulate without cleanup, consuming disk over time.

**Current state (2026-04-26):**
- Staging: 3 release dirs × 214 MB = 642 MB at `/home/deploy/projects/voice-clone-staging/frontend/releases/`
- Prod: 4 release dirs (~213 MB each = ~850 MB) at `/home/deploy/projects/voice-clone/frontend/releases/`
- Disk usage: 76% (729G/968G on /dev/vda1)

Not urgent — disk has 239G headroom. But every deploy adds ~214 MB and old dirs are never reaped.

**Proposed fix:**
Add a `keep_last_n=5` cleanup step at the end of `scripts/deploy-staging-frontend.sh` and `scripts/deploy-frontend.sh`:

```bash
# Keep last N releases, delete the rest
RELEASES_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/frontend/releases"
KEEP=5
ls -t "$RELEASES_DIR" | tail -n +$((KEEP + 1)) | xargs -I{} rm -rf "$RELEASES_DIR/{}"
```

Or a cron with similar logic in `infra/systemd/voice-clone-cleanup-releases.timer`.

**Acceptance:**
- Cleanup runs after every deploy
- N most recent releases kept (allows quick rollback)
- Tested on staging first
- Doesn't delete the `current` symlink target

**Out of scope:**
- Cleanup of /data/voice-clone-staging/storage/next-cache (Next.js manages its own size)
- Backup directory cleanup (separate retention policy)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Deploy scripts (staging + prod) auto-prune old releases keeping last 5
- [ ] OR systemd timer with same logic
- [ ] Verified `current` symlink target is never touched
- [ ] Tested on staging first (one full deploy cycle confirms cleanup runs)

title: Phase 3: WebGL Neural Field Background
description:
WebGL background effect for portfolio.

**Concept:** Neural Field - reactive particle/noise field

**Option A: GPU Particles with R3F (Recommended)**
- @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei
- Thousands of particles forming subtle grid
- Particles drift with Perlin noise
- Cursor proximity causes scatter/attract
- Color shift from Void Navy to Cyber Lime near cursor

**Option B: Shader-Only (Lighter)**
- Single fullscreen canvas with GLSL fragment shader
- Animated noise field (reactive)
- Cursor creates ripples
- Smaller bundle size

**Performance:**
- Use OffscreenCanvas where supported
- Cap at 30fps for background
- Disable on prefers-reduced-motion
- Lazy load (don't block initial paint)

**Reference:** docs/FEATURE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Section 4
